- IMU-visual sensor fusion

Sensor fusion combines visual features with inertial measurements to improve pose estimation stability and handle challenging lighting conditions.

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses understanding of edge-optimized neural rendering, real-time perception under occlusion, and rapid on-device adaptation for dynamic industrial environments.

## Key Concepts
- Real-time monocular NeRF for dynamic scene reconstruction
- Edge GPU latency constraints (sub-60ms per frame)
- 5-shot on-device meta-learning adaptation
- Occlusion-robust 6-DoF pose estimation
- Shelf/worker segmentation
- Domain randomization with synthetic+real data fusion

## Code Example
```python
# High-level on-device adaptation using MAML-style optimization
def adapt_on_device(model, new_frames, num_shots=5):
    \"\"\"Perform 5-shot adaptation on edge device.\"\"\"
    adapted_model = copy.deepcopy(model)
    support_set = new_frames[:num_shots]
    
    for step in range(adapter_steps):
        loss = compute_meta_loss(adapted_model, support_set)
        grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, adapted_model.parameters())
        adapted_model = apply_gradients(adapted_model, grads, lr=adapt_lr)
    
    return adapted_model
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design a monocular, edge-optimized computer vision system that reasons about 3D structure and object interactions within cluttered environments, with rapid adaptation to novel furniture categories.

## Key Concepts

- Monocular 3D pose estimation in cluttered environments
- Scene graphs and graph neural networks for relational reasoning
- Grasp affordances for robotic manipulation
- On-device meta-learning (3-shot adaptation)
- Synthetic-to-real domain transfer strategies

## Code Example

```python
# Pseudo-code: update_scene_graph for a frame
def update_scene_graph(frame, model, device='cuda'):
    features = model.backbone(frame)
    detections = model.detector(features)
    poses = model.pose_head(features, detections)
    scene_graph = model.gnn_head(detections, poses)
    affordances = model.affordance_head(features, detections)
    return {
        'objects': detections,
        'poses': poses,
        'relations': scene_graph,
        'affordances': affordances
    }
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses end-to-end design for real-world inventory sensing under occlusion, speed, and lighting variation, emphasizing self-supervised depth, differentiable 3D reasoning, and uncertainty estimation on edge hardware.

## Key Concepts
- Lightweight 2D detector (EfficientDet)
- Self-supervised depth from ego-motion
- Differentiable 3D box regression
- Uncertainty via MC dropout and aleatoric depth
- Kalman tracking + data association
- Edge deployment (latency, memory)

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode
function pipeline(frame, state){
  proposals = detector(frame)
  depth = depthFromMotion(frame, state)
  boxes = reg3D(proposals, depth)
  tracks = kalmanTrack(boxes, state)
  return tracks
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you evaluate robustness to motion blur and occlusion?
- How would you adapt the system to different pallet shapes/sizes or new warehouses without labeled data?
